important.name: Session-cwd test leaves the hook process cwd at the project root
important.summary: test_file_project_wins_over_the_session_cwd sets only the payload cwd to tmp_path; _call always runs the hook subprocess with cwd=root (line 29 passes `root` to _run). In a real session the process cwd and the payload cwd are both the session cwd. A regression that resolved the project from os.getcwd() (the hook's last fallback in _config_for) before the file's directory would still find the project and deny, so the test cannot catch it.
fix: In _call, run the hook with the session cwd as the process cwd too: `return _run(json.dumps(payload), cwd or root)`.
Or add a dedicated test that calls _run(json.dumps(payload), tmp_path) with the payload cwd also set to tmp_path and asserts the deny.

Also (system_shape): README.md:185-186 says the hook denies hand edits of the saved .txt files; the matcher is Write|Edit only. Bash redirects, heredocs and PowerShell writes pass, and c-msg/SKILL.md:74 names heredoc and > as hand-writing routes.

Also (overall): README and the agent-permissions table say the hook denies hand edits of the saved .txt files, but it is matched only to Write|Edit. A denied session can still rewrite the TXT with a Bash heredoc or redirect, or PowerShell Set-Content (the forms the c-msg Common Mistakes table lists), so the stated guarantee is broader than the enforcement.
fix: Reword to 'denies Write and Edit tool calls on the saved .txt files' in README.md:185-186 and in the agent-permissions table row
Reword to: denies Write and Edit tool calls on the saved .txt files; note in the hook docstring that shell writes are left to the standing rule.

Or extend enforcement: have bash_discipline and powershell_allow_shapes deny a redirect or Set-Content/Out-File whose target is a guarded TXT (reuse guarded()).

minor.name: Docstring promises a payload-cwd fallback the code effectively never takes
minor.summary:
The module docstring (lines 10-11) and _config_for say the project is the target file's nearest existing directory, else the payload cwd. _existing_dir walks path.parents, which always ends at the drive/root anchor, so for any absolute path on an existing volume it returns a directory and the cwd branch is dead. When that directory is outside every git repo, project_root falls back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (then the directory itself), not the payload cwd, so the stated fallback order is wrong.

Also (runtime): The hook is registered for `Write|Edit` only, so `sed -i`, a heredoc redirect, `python -c` or PowerShell Set-Content on <branch>.txt still lands. The deny reason tells the session the file is final, but a session that treats the denial as a tool obstacle can retry through the shell, which is the exact unasked rewrite the guard exists to stop. The docstring is accurate about scope, so this is a coverage gap rather than a contract break.
fix: Reword the docstrings: the project is the git top level of the target's nearest existing directory, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else that directory (project_root's order); drop the cwd branch or keep it only for a path whose anchor does not exist.
Alternatively pass the payload cwd to project_root when _git_toplevel of the nearest directory fails, to make the documented fallback real.
Document the gap in the module docstring and README line 185-186 (guard covers the file tools only).

Or add a Bash/PowerShell check (in bash_discipline.py or a sibling) that denies commands naming a .txt under artifacts.commit_messages with a write operator (>, >>, sed -i, tee, Set-Content, Out-File), reusing REASON.

minor.name: Guard spawns git and loads config on every Write/Edit before the cheap name check
minor.summary:
main() calls _config_for (nearest-dir walk, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocess, load_config, activate) for every Write or Edit payload, and only then does guarded() reject non-.txt names. Every file edit in every session pays a git process plus a config parse (noticeable on Windows) to answer a question the filename alone settles for nearly all calls; a broken harness.json is also reparsed on each edit.

Also (overall): main() calls _config_for (git rev-parse via project_root, harness.json read, jsonschema validation) for every Write or Edit in every session, and only then does guarded() reject a non-.txt name. Nearly all edits target .py/.md files, so each one pays the config load and a git subprocess for nothing; the suffix and PR<NNN>_merge.txt checks need no config.
fix: In main(), return 0 before _config_for unless file_path.name.lower().endswith('.txt') and not _MERGE_TXT.match(file_path.name); e.g. split the name test out of guarded() into a _txt_candidate(path) helper and call it first.
In main(), return 0 before _config_for when file_path.name.lower() does not end with .txt or _MERGE_TXT matches it (split a name-only predicate out of guarded() and call it first).
Add a test that a .py Write produces no output, so the fast path stays covered.

minor.name: CHANGE_ROUTE names no capture arguments, so it misses a --base TXT
minor.summary:
The route harness:amend-commit-msg -- <change> (relayed verbatim via FINAL_LINE, hook REASON, HARNESS_RULES.md:34) targets <branch>.txt; a --base draft lives in <branch>_<sha7>.txt and needs --base <sha7> (amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md:40-44).

Also (docs, overall): The B1 rule (and the receipt's FINAL_LINE / hook REASON, all built from CHANGE_ROUTE) names 'harness:amend-commit-msg -- <change>' as the route for a branch TXT. A branch-commit-msg run with --base REF saves <branch>_<sha7>.txt, and amend-commit-msg only targets that file when given the same --base (amend SKILL.md Step 1). Followed literally after a --base draft, the stated route amends <branch>.txt when one exists (the wrong ledger) or exits 'no TXT to amend'.

Also (overall): The B1 bullet covers only When harness:c-msg or harness:branch-commit-msg returns. harness:amend-commit-msg also finishes with branch_commit_msg.py build and prints the same receipt ending in FINAL_LINE, but the standing rule does not tell the main session to relay that receipt and the amended TXT unchanged, so a post-amend rewrite in chat falls outside the rule.

Also (runtime): FINAL_LINE and the guard REASON both end with the static CHANGE_ROUTE `harness:amend-commit-msg -- <change> for a branch TXT`. For a build that wrote <branch>_<sha7>.txt (a --base skeleton) or a denied Edit of that file, following the route literally captures --edit against <branch>.txt: it amends the wrong draft when a branch TXT exists, or fails with `no TXT to amend`. amend-commit-msg only recovers by suggesting --base <sha7> after the failure.
fix: Make CHANGE_ROUTE read harness:amend-commit-msg [--base <sha7>] -- <change> and mirror it in HARNESS_RULES.md:33-34.

Extend CHANGE_ROUTE to 'harness:amend-commit-msg [--base <sha7>] -- <change> for a branch TXT (the --base the draft used)' and update the rule text in HARNESS_RULES.md so test_rules_keep_drafted_commit_messages still matches
Alternatively have the receipt for a --base run print the exact amend command with that sha7, and say so in the rule

Name harness:amend-commit-msg in the bullet (When harness:c-msg, harness:branch-commit-msg or harness:amend-commit-msg returns) and extend test_rules_keep_drafted_commit_messages to assert it; keep the file under RULES_LIMIT.
Have receipt() append the base hint when the payload carries txt_suffix (e.g. `harness:amend-commit-msg --base <sha7> -- <change>`), passing the suffix from _cmd_build.
Or extend CHANGE_ROUTE to read `harness:amend-commit-msg [--base <sha7>] -- <change>` so the route names the based form; HARNESS_RULES.md and the drift tests follow the constant.

minor.name: Guard hook's documented fail-open and case rules have no test
minor.summary:
The hook docstring promises that an unusable harness config never blocks, _file_path refuses a relative file_path, and guarded() matches `.txt` and `PR<N>_merge.txt` case-insensitively. The test module covers garbage stdin and a missing file_path only; a malformed .claude/harness.json, a relative file_path, `B.TXT` and `pr12_MERGE.txt` are unpinned, so a change that blocks on a bad config or drops the case folding passes the suite.

Also (overall): The hook docstring promises an unusable harness config never blocks, and _config_for catches ConfigError/OSError for that, but test_guard_commit_txt.py only covers non-JSON stdin and a payload without file_path. A regression that lets a malformed .claude/harness.json raise (exit 1, an error on every Write/Edit) or deny would pass the suite.
fix: Add tests: a project whose .claude/harness.json is invalid JSON (files={'.claude/harness.json': '{'}) is not denied; a payload with a relative file_path is not denied; `docs/_commit_messages/B.TXT` is denied; `docs/_commit_messages/pr12_MERGE.txt` is allowed.
Add a test: make_project with a .claude/harness.json holding invalid JSON (or an unknown key), Edit on docs/_commit_messages/b.txt, assert returncode 0 and empty stdout.

Add a test that imports CHANGE_ROUTE and asserts it contains `harness:c-msg <change>` while the c-msg argument-hint takes a free-text change, and that the amend-commit-msg argument-hint carries `-- <`.
Move a `skill_parts(path) -> Tuple[Dict[str, str], str]` helper into tests/lib (beside _commit_helpers) and import it from both modules.
